purpose: Teach: 重厚/緑茶/木星/レンガ/交響楽/ブドウ/焼き鳥/安楽

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが重厚な書斎の家具を選ばれたぞ
lines.en: You know, when I was young, Father chose those heavy study furnishings.
lines.style: Gentle, distant memory-voice. Soft attack on the opening. Slow, measured pace. Each image placed carefully, like arranging things on a shelf. Slight reverence for the father.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、毎朝緑茶を入れてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes… and your grandfather used to brew green tea every morning, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, collaborative remembering. Light, conversational lilt on the opening. Inviting him to agree. Soft affection in 'dear'—not condescending, just intimate. Gentle rise at the question mark.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが木星の観測会に行かれたぞ
lines.en: When I was young, Father used to attend those Jupiter observation nights.
lines.style: Same wistful distance as before. Quiet reverence. Slightly slower on 'Jupiter'—letting the image linger. Sparing, economical delivery. The tone of someone narrating their own memory to themselves.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、レンガ造りのお家にも住まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you lived in that lovely brick house once too, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Genuine delight in the detail. Rises slightly on 'brick house'—that particular memory pleases her. Soft, almost musical. The 'dear' carries recognition, like she's checking in with him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが交響楽の演奏会に通われたぞ
lines.en: In those days, Father would go to symphony concerts regularly.
lines.style: Wistful, but with quiet pride now. Slightly more confident than the earlier lines. Lets 'symphony' breathe—that was a cultured household. Still measured, still distant, but the rhythm is settled.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、秋はブドウ狩りに連れて行ってくださったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you took me grape-picking every autumn, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warmth with a touch of longing underneath. 'Grape-picking' rises slightly—a tender autumn ritual. The 'you took me' shifts into her voice, not his memory. Soft fadeout on 'dear'—reaching across time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと焼き鳥屋で乾杯したぞ
lines.en: When I was young, Father and I would raise our glasses together at the yakitori place.
lines.style: Wistful and intimate together now. Warmth in 'Father and I'—a moment of real closeness. Lighter attack, almost conversational. The toast itself carries quiet significance. Slight lift at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭で安楽椅子に座られてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you'd sit in that armchair in the garden, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Tender, content. Visual and present—she can still see him there. Soft attack on 'armchair.' The whole line settles into warmth. 'Dear' carries the weight of long habit and real love. Trails off very gently.
